From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order form redlines — SLA & maintenance windows

Camila / team — I reviewed Zenotech’s comments. Below are the legal-friendly redlines I suggest we propose back (draft language included). I prioritized clarity and operational alignment so we don’t leave a lot of ambiguous interpretation for billing/procurement later.

1) Uptime target and measurement
Proposed: "Service Availability" means the percentage of time the Service is available for inbound requests measured monthly. Redwood’s target for Service Availability is 99.95% per calendar month. Measurement excludes scheduled maintenance windows that were communicated in advance as set forth in Section X.
Rationale: 99.95% is standard for this tier and keeps our existing capacity SLAs intact. If Zenotech requires a higher number we should route to sales leadership for discounted pricing.

2) Response times (incidents)
Proposed table to insert into Support Terms:
- Priority 1 (Production P1): Initial response within 1 hour; remediation target 8 hours for standard incidents where workaround or mitigation is possible.
- Priority 2 (Degraded service): Initial response within 4 hours; remediation target 48 hours.
- Priority 3 (Information request / non-incident): Initial response within 24 hours.
Rationale: 30m initial response is operationally aggressive and would require an SRE on-call guarantee and a pricing change. We can offer 1 hour as a compromise.

3) Maintenance windows and blackout periods
Proposed: Scheduled maintenance will be notified 7 calendar days in advance and will only occur during the customer’s selected maintenance window. Redwood will offer a weekly 4-hour maintenance window outside customer business hours (default: Saturdays 02:00–06:00 PT). For customers that require blackout restrictions (no maintenance Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 PT), we can include that as an exception in the Order Form but it may reduce available maintenance capacity and could affect availability guarantees.

4) Service credits and cap
Proposed: Service credits shall be calculated per calendar month as a percentage of the monthly service fees for the affected service. Credits for an availability failure will be: 10% of monthly fees for availability between 99.5%–99.95%, 25% for availability between 98.0%–99.5%, and 50% for availability below 98.0%. The cumulative credit for any calendar month shall not exceed 100% of the monthly fees for the affected service. Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for availability failures.

5) Auditability and evidence
Add: "Customer must submit an SLA claim within 30 days of the end of the month and include reasonable evidence (request ids, timestamps, impacted zones). Redwood will provide a report within 15 business days of claim receipt."

Attachments: I produced a tracked-redline PDF (Zenotech_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) and a simple SLA-exception-matrix.xlsx showing trade-offs if Zenotech requests blackout windows during business hours.

If folks are aligned I can send this as our official counter to Samir.

-Lauren

--

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order form redlines — SLA & maintenance windows

Fyi — ops notes on Lauren’s draft:
- P1 remediation target of 8 hours presumes we have prefix cache and prioritized routing for Zenotech traffic; we should flag this requirement in the Order Form. If they want 4-hour remediation we’ll need to reserve dedicated capacity (Dedicated offering) or a monthly uplift.
- For blackout windows: we can accept "no scheduled maintenance" Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 PT but only if they accept a monthly maintenance window that is at least 6 hours outside their business hours. Operationally we need a single recurring slot to do OS/kernel updates.
- On evidence: include a clause that Redwood’s internal monitor and request-id correlation will be the primary source for incident timing; customer logs are useful but must match request ids.

I also think we should offer a one-time "onboarding SLA validation" where our SRE team runs a simulated failover with Zenotech during their onboarding week — makes them comfortable and reduces churn.

-Markus

--
Markus Klein
Senior Director, Service Reliability
markus@redwood.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@zenotech.com>

Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redlines — SLA & maintenance windows (consolidated counter)

Samir — thanks for the patience. Attached is our consolidated counter-proposal (Zenotech_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) with the key items summarized below so procurement has a single reference: 

Summary of key counters:
- Service Availability: 99.95% monthly (measurement excludes scheduled maintenance).
- Incidents / Support response: P1 initial response 1 hour; remediation target 8 hours (standard); P2 initial response 4 hours; P3 24 hours.
- Maintenance: We propose a recurring 4-hour weekly maintenance window by default (Sat 02:00–06:00 PT). We can accept a contract exception for no maintenance Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 PT if Zenotech accepts a single monthly 6-hour slot outside business hours and acknowledges this may affect rapid security patching speed.
- Service credits: Tiered monthly credit schedule (10% / 25% / 50%) with a monthly cap equal to 100% of the affected monthly fees. Credits are the exclusive monetary remedy.
- Evidence & claims: Customer must submit SLA claim within 30 days; Redwood will provide supporting report within 15 business days. Primary measurement will be Redwood’s request-id correlation logs.

Operational note: Markus will run an onboarding SLA validation session (optional) during the first month; we’re happy to schedule this.

Next steps: If this looks acceptable we can prepare an Exec-approved Order Form to attach to the MSA and route to DocuSign. If Zenotech needs the 30m P1 initial response or to remove the credit cap we will need to update pricing or move to Dedicated capacity — I can brief my manager for approvals if you confirm that ask.

If you’d like to talk through line-by-line I’m available Friday 9/10 10:00am PT. Otherwise please confirm whether procurement is comfortable with the single-page credit schedule and the blackout exception trade-off.

Thanks,
Camila

--
